old_caption: The video begins with a first-person perspective from inside a kayak, showing the bow cutting through choppy waters. The kayak is orange with black markings, and the paddle is visible, dipping into the water. As the kayak moves forward, the camera pans slightly to reveal a rugged, rocky coastline on one side and an expansive body of water stretching out towards the horizon under a cloudy sky. The waves continue to roll, creating a dynamic and immersive experience. The camera captures the motion of the kayak as it navigates through the water, emphasizing the interaction between the boat and the powerful waves.
original_wisa_caption: The video begins with a dramatic close-up shot of a massive wave crashing down, its white foam billowing into the air. The camera then transitions to a first-person perspective from inside a kayak, showing the bow cutting through choppy waters. The kayak is orange with black markings, and the paddle is visible, dipping into the water. As the kayak moves forward, the camera pans slightly to reveal a rugged, rocky coastline on one side and an expansive body of water stretching out towards the horizon under a cloudy sky. The waves continue to roll, creating a dynamic and immersive experience. The camera captures the motion of the kayak as it navigates through the water, emphasizing the interaction between the boat and the powerful waves. The scene concludes with the kayak approaching another large wave, hinting at more adventure ahead.
caption: A first-person view from an orange sea kayak shows dark, choppy water with patches of white foam and a large rocky headland on the right under a flat gray sky. A black Werner paddle blade is raised at the left side, then moves downward and exits the frame while the kayak bow bobs near the bottom center. The orange bow remains visible throughout, rising and falling relative to the camera as the vessel rides the swell. The horizon and cliff edge tilt and drift slightly as the camera rolls and yaws with the water, rather than the scenery moving. White foam in the foreground continuously reshapes and redistributes across the dark surface, while a dark swell line in the mid-distance shifts with the view. After the paddle leaves view, the scene continues without it for a long interval. Later, a small black edge re-enters at the lower left and remains visible through the end while the kayak keeps bobbing.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
